images.caption: Beach of Madras, c. 1851. Hand-coloured salt print of an unidentified colonial building on the Madras foreshore, Bay of Bengal beyond.
images.credit: Frederick Fiebig, c. 1851. British Library / Wikimedia Commons.
images.license: Public domain (pre-1931 publication; copyright expired under Indian Copyright Act, 1957)

images.caption: Plan of the town of Madras and its limits, surveyed in 1822 for the Justices in Sessions. Shows the walled Fort, Black Town, the Cooum river, and the elongated tank polygons (Long Tank, Spur Tank, Nungambakkam Tank, Mylapore Tank) that defined the early-19th-century city's western and southern boundary.
images.credit: Captain W. Ravenshaw, surveyor; engraved by J. Walker, 1822.
images.license: Public domain (pre-1931 publication; author's life plus 70 years expired)
images.note: Original Wikimedia file is 113 MB. Resized to 2400px wide with macOS sips for web delivery.

images.caption: Pallikaranai marsh, April 2022, photographed from the southern bank in Sholinganallur. Greater flamingoes in the foreground, IT park reflected in the water behind.
images.note: Resized to 2400px wide with macOS sips for web delivery.

images.caption: Puzhal (Red Hills) reservoir, one of Chennai's four main supply lakes, on 31 May 2018. Acquired by the Operational Land Imager on Landsat 8. The reservoir is at near-full capacity.
images.credit: NASA Earth Observatory image by Lauren Dauphin, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey.
images.note: Resized to 2400px wide with macOS sips for web delivery.

images.caption: Same Puzhal reservoir, 19 June 2019, the morning Chennai was officially declared dry. Combined storage across all four city reservoirs was about a tenth of one per cent of capacity. The dark water of 2018 has been replaced by exposed earth.
images.credit: NASA Earth Observatory image by Lauren Dauphin, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey.
